lines.text: Three whole-number sides that add up to twenty-four. How many different triangles can you make?
lines.caption: Three whole-number sides that add up to twenty-four. How many different triangles can you make?

lines.text: Missing just one or two is the classic slip. I'm Vantee, and we'll find every single one!
lines.caption: Missing just one or two is the classic slip. I'm Vantee, and we'll find every single one!

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: How many different triangles have whole-number side lengths and a perimeter of twenty-four?
lines.caption: How many different triangles have whole-number side lengths and a perimeter of twenty-four?

lines.text: Triangles with the same three side lengths count once. Here are the five choices.
lines.caption: Triangles with the same three side lengths count once. Here are the five choices.

lines.text: We need three whole numbers that add up to twenty-four. Each one is a side.
lines.caption: We need three whole numbers that add up to twenty-four. Each one is a side.

lines.text: But not every three numbers make a triangle. Two, two and twenty can't close up.
lines.caption: But not every three numbers make a triangle. Two, two and twenty can't close up.

lines.text: And order doesn't matter. Seven, eight, nine is the same triangle as nine, eight, seven.
lines.caption: And order doesn't matter. Seven, eight, nine is the same triangle as nine, eight, seven.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! First, the triangle rule.
lines.caption: Welcome back! First, the triangle rule.

lines.text: The two shorter sides must add up to MORE than the longest side, or they can't meet.
lines.caption: The two shorter sides must add up to MORE than the longest side, or they can't meet.

lines.text: If they only tie, the triangle squashes flat into a line.
lines.caption: If they only tie, the triangle squashes flat into a line.

lines.text: Now here's the trick. The two shorter sides make up the rest of the perimeter.
lines.caption: Now here's the trick. The two shorter sides make up the rest of the perimeter.

lines.text: So the longest side must be shorter than half the perimeter. Half of twenty-four is twelve.
lines.caption: So the longest side must be shorter than half the perimeter. Half of twenty-four is twelve.

lines.text: If the longest side is under twelve, the other sides always fit. So that's our only test.
lines.caption: If the longest side is under twelve, the other sides always fit. So that's our only test.

lines.text: How short can the longest side be? If it were seven, all three sides would be seven or less.
lines.caption: How short can the longest side be? If it were seven, all three sides would be seven or less.

lines.text: Seven plus seven plus seven is only twenty-one. Too short! So the longest side is at least eight.
lines.caption: Seven plus seven plus seven is only twenty-one. Too short! So the longest side is at least eight.

lines.text: So the longest side is eight, nine, ten or eleven. Let's make a list for each one.
lines.caption: So the longest side is eight, nine, ten or eleven. Let's make a list for each one.

lines.text: Longest side eleven. The other two sides add up to thirteen.
lines.caption: Longest side eleven. The other two sides add up to thirteen.

lines.text: The middle side can't be more than eleven. So we start with two and eleven.
lines.caption: The middle side can't be more than eleven. So we start with two and eleven.

lines.text: Then three and ten, four and nine, five and eight, six and seven. That's five triangles.
lines.caption: Then three and ten, four and nine, five and eight, six and seven. That's five triangles.

lines.text: Why stop there? Next is seven and six, which is six and seven again.
lines.caption: Why stop there? Next is seven and six, which is six and seven again.

lines.text: Longest side ten. The other two add up to fourteen, so we start with four and ten.
lines.caption: Longest side ten. The other two add up to fourteen, so we start with four and ten.

lines.text: Then five and nine, six and eight, seven and seven. That's four triangles.
lines.caption: Then five and nine, six and eight, seven and seven. That's four triangles.

lines.text: Longest side nine. The rest adds up to fifteen: six and nine, then seven and eight. That's two.
lines.caption: Longest side nine. The rest adds up to fifteen: six and nine, then seven and eight. That's two.

lines.text: Longest side eight. The other two add up to sixteen. Only eight and eight fits. That's one!
lines.caption: Longest side eight. The other two add up to sixteen. Only eight and eight fits. That's one!

lines.text: Five, plus four, plus two, plus one. That's twelve triangles! The answer is C.
lines.caption: Five, plus four, plus two, plus one. That's twelve triangles! The answer is C.

lines.text: Here's a clever second way. Measure how far each side is from twelve, half the perimeter. Call it the gap.
lines.caption: Here's a clever second way. Measure how far each side is from twelve, half the perimeter. Call it the gap.

lines.text: Take seven, eight, nine. The gaps are five, four and three.
lines.caption: Take seven, eight, nine. The gaps are five, four and three.

lines.text: Three twelves make thirty-six. The sides use twenty-four. So the gaps always add up to twelve.
lines.caption: Three twelves make thirty-six. The sides use twenty-four. So the gaps always add up to twelve.

lines.text: Every gap is at least one, because every side is less than twelve.
lines.caption: Every gap is at least one, because every side is less than twelve.

lines.text: It works backwards too. Gaps that add up to twelve give sides under twelve, so a real triangle.
lines.caption: It works backwards too. Gaps that add up to twelve give sides under twelve, so a real triangle.

lines.text: So we count the ways to split twelve into three whole numbers, each at least one.
lines.caption: So we count the ways to split twelve into three whole numbers, each at least one.

lines.text: A biggest gap of ten gives one way. Nine, one way. Eight, two ways. Seven, two ways.
lines.caption: A biggest gap of ten gives one way. Nine, one way. Eight, two ways. Seven, two ways.

lines.text: Six, three ways. Five, two ways. And four, four, four is one more.
lines.caption: Six, three ways. Five, two ways. And four, four, four is one more.

lines.text: One plus one plus two plus two plus three plus two plus one. Twelve again!
lines.caption: One plus one plus two plus two plus three plus two plus one. Twelve again!

lines.text: When would you pick this one? It's a great double-check on your list.
lines.caption: When would you pick this one? It's a great double-check on your list.

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Ten is what you'd get if you left out the longest side of nine. Those two triangles go missing.
lines.caption: Ten is what you'd get if you left out the longest side of nine. Those two triangles go missing.

lines.text: Eleven is what you'd get if you forgot eight, eight, eight. An equilateral triangle still counts!
lines.caption: Eleven is what you'd get if you forgot eight, eight, eight. An equilateral triangle still counts!

lines.text: Thirteen is what you'd get if one triangle is counted twice, in a different order.
lines.caption: Thirteen is what you'd get if one triangle is counted twice, in a different order.

lines.text: And nineteen is just too many. Our full list has only twelve.
lines.caption: And nineteen is just too many. Our full list has only twelve.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Pick the longest side first, then list the other two in order.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Pick the longest side first, then list the other two in order.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Same question, new perimeter.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Same question, new perimeter.

lines.text: How many different triangles have whole-number side lengths and a perimeter of twenty?
lines.caption: How many different triangles have whole-number side lengths and a perimeter of twenty?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. Half of twenty is ten. So the longest side is less than ten.
lines.caption: Let's check. Half of twenty is ten. So the longest side is less than ten.

lines.text: Six plus six plus six is only eighteen. So the longest side is at least seven.
lines.caption: Six plus six plus six is only eighteen. So the longest side is at least seven.

lines.text: Longest side nine. The other two add up to eleven.
lines.caption: Longest side nine. The other two add up to eleven.

lines.text: Two and nine, three and eight, four and seven, five and six. That's four.
lines.caption: Two and nine, three and eight, four and seven, five and six. That's four.

lines.text: Longest side eight. The rest is twelve: four and eight, five and seven, six and six. That's three.
lines.caption: Longest side eight. The rest is twelve: four and eight, five and seven, six and six. That's three.

lines.text: Longest side seven. The rest is thirteen. Only six and seven works. That's one.
lines.caption: Longest side seven. The rest is thirteen. Only six and seven works. That's one.

lines.text: Notice there's no equilateral this time. Twenty can't split into three equal whole numbers.
lines.caption: Notice there's no equilateral this time. Twenty can't split into three equal whole numbers.

lines.text: Four, plus three, plus one. That's eight triangles! If you found eight, amazing work!
lines.caption: Four, plus three, plus one. That's eight triangles! If you found eight, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: The longest side must be shorter than half the perimeter, since the other two must add up to more.
lines.caption: The longest side must be shorter than half the perimeter, since the other two must add up to more.

lines.text: So pick the longest side first, find its limits, then list the other two in order.
lines.caption: So pick the longest side first, find its limits, then list the other two in order.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
